 VEGAS MUSIC NEWS: ‘When We Were Young’ Back, Animated K-Pop Band, Former Beatle Residency?
 Posted on : 
 November 18, 2026, 02:05h.
 Last updated on : 
 November 19, 2026, 05:26h.
 Written by 
 Corey Levitan 
 Corey Levitan joined Casino.org in 2022 after a long career covering Las Vegas. He currently covers entertainment, dining and gaming news in Las Vegas... 
 Click for more 
 Key Points
 Blink-182 and Pierce the Veil will co-headline the "When We Were Young" festival on Oct. 16, 2027
 Animated K-pop trio Huntr/x will somehow bring its Golden World Tour to T-Mobile Arena
 A strong industry rumor has Ringo Starr momentarily announcing the first Las Vegas residency ever by a Beatle
 Share 
 Add to Preferred Sources 
 “When We Were Young” will return to the Las Vegas Festival Grounds for the fifth time on Oct. 16, 2027, with Blink-182 co-headlining for the third time (along with Pierce the Veil) . The massive punk, emo and alternative-rock festival skipped 2026.
 Mark Hoppus, Travis Barker, and Tom DeLonge of Blink-182 perform in May 2026 in L.A. The San Diego band also headlined “When We Were Young” in 2023 (along with Green Day ) and 2025. (Image: Christopher Polk/WWD via Getty) 
 The 2027 bill will also feature Limp Bizkit, Third Eye Blind, The Used, All Time Low, Simple Plan, 5 Seconds of Summer, Circa Survive, Taking Back Sunday, Sleeping With Sirens, Explosions in the Sky and Portugal, among dozens of other rock acts.
 Once more, the gathering will spread more than 50 performances across four stages. And its diverse offerings will stretch from singer-songwriters ( Michelle Branch, Natasha Bedingfield, and Ashlee Simpson — yes, Ashlee Simpson! ) to metalcore ( Underoath, Poison the Well, Stick to Your Guns, and Drain ).
In February 2026, organizers announced that the festival would take this year off, providing only the cryptic reason “to give this festival the care it deserves and to make sure what comes next feels just as special as what came before.” (Industry observers suspected factors including renewed competition from the revived “ Warped Tour” and rising production and insurance costs.)
 The festival presale begins at 10 a.m. PT Friday, Nov. 20. Fans can sign up to receive a passcode at whenwewereyoungfestival.com. A general on-sale follows on the same day at 11 a.m., if any tickets remain.
 Drawing a Crowd
 Netflix’s animated sensation “K-Pop Demon Hunters” is jumping from the screen to the stage, with the fictional K-pop trio Huntr/X headlining a pair of performances (including a matinee show) on Aug. 7, 2027, at T-Mobile Arena. It’s part of the fictional band’s first real tour , the “Golden World Tour.”
 The K-Pop Demon Hunters band features Rumi, Mira, and Zoey. (Image: AEG Presents) 
 Pop music has a long history of fictional pop bands filling real arenas. The ’60s had The Monkees, the ’70s had the Blues Brothers , and the ’90s had Spinal Tap. But large-scale arena tours built around fictional characters have been relatively rare in the modern era. And the concept has never been executed like this…
Rather than featuring human performers impersonating the animated characters, the production will combine animation, live-action performers, stunts, and interactive technology to bring Huntr/X members Rumi, Mira, and Zoey into the arena.
 The tour takes its name from “Golden,” the group’s breakout hit, which became the first K-pop song to win both an Oscar and a Grammy. The track also spent eight weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned 5x Platinum certification.
 A fan presale will begin at 10 a.m. PT later today (Thursday, Nov. 19). Fans can register for access at kpopdemonhunterstour.com. Remaining tickets are scheduled to go on sale to the general public at 10 a.m. Friday, Nov. 20.
 Whispered This Week…
 A rumor circulating in the Vegas entertainment industry suggests that the first Las Vegas residency for a former Beatle is about to be announced shortly. Might Ringo Starr & His All-Starr Band be headed for a run at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace in 2027? We’ll let you know for sure when we can.
